records.title: Who is doing this, and on whose money
records.summary: Who runs Lubbock
records.text: About this chapter | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Lubbock, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → About · Lubbock, TX Who is doing this, and on whose money This is the Lubbock chapter of the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It is independent of the City of Lubbock, of Lubbock County, and of the State of Texas. It takes no money from any of them. How we source claims Every factual claim on this site links to a primary document or to a named outlet. Where a document exists, we publish the document rather than our description of it. We never invent a government phone number, address or docket number. Every contact datum is transcribed from an official published source and dated on the page. If we have not transcribed it yet, the page says so and links to the city's own directory instead of guessing. Every external link is fetched before it is published , and re-checked automatically every week. The result of that check is public on the automation page . Sources for this chapter were last verified 2026-07-26 . We publish released records whole. No redaction of a public record the government has already released. We never allege a crime. We publish the document, the amount and the date, and let readers and prosecutors do their own jobs. A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in file metadata. We link out to local news and never republish it. What this chapter is not It is not a newspaper, not a campaign, and not aligned with any candidate, party or slate. It does not endorse. Its output is records, an archive, and the plain fact of whether a public body answered a lawful request on time. Funding The Foundation is funded by individual donations. Records cost money — Texas allows a body to charge for search and copying under § 552.2615, and a single large request can run into real numbers. Donations pay those invoices, the servers that hold the archive, and nothing else. Contributions are tax-deductible. Zelle: team@moveweight.com . Financial disclosures and the Form 990 are published by the Foundation at foundation.moveweight.com . Corrections If something here is wrong, we want to fix it and we will say that we did. Send the correction and, if you have it, the document — here . A correction is never quietly edited in; the change and its date stay on the page. Contact Records and requests: foia@moveweight.com Everything else: expose@moveweight.net

This page reports what actually happened, including when it failed. A site that quietly rots looks identical to one that is current, right up until somebody relies on it. So the status below is generated by the jobs themselves — it is not maintained by hand and cannot be made to look better than it is. It never logs in, never submits anything, and never touches a page the city has not made public. Link check. Re-fetches every external link this chapter publishes. Cities move pages, and a records-request link that 404s fails a reader at the exact moment they were about to act. Search index. Rebuilds the site's index from the pages and the extracted agenda text, so a resident can search a phrase and land on the agenda that carried it. Nothing writes to a government system. Records requests are sent by a person, deliberately, never by a timer. If a job has been red for a while That is a bug, not a policy. Tell us — the whole point of publishing this page is that somebody outside the project can see the failure before we do.

records.title: Every official link, in one place
records.summary: Verified links to Lubbock city government, Lubbock County offices, records portals, budgets and Texas oversight bodies. Checked 2026-07-26.
records.text: Lubbock City Desk — every official link in one place | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content Records & transparency Open records requests Lubbock's GovQA portal — where a Texas Public Information Act request to the City is filed and tracked. https://lubbocktx.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/supporthome.aspx County & state Lubbock County https://www.lubbockcounty.gov/ Texas AG — Open Government https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/open-government Texas oversight Where a Lubbock decision gets reviewed by somebody who does not work for Lubbock. Texas Attorney General — Open Government A body that wants to withhold must ask the AG within 10 business days. Those rulings are public and searchable, and they are the single best record of what a city tried to hide. Texas Comptroller — Transparency Local government debt, tax rates and economic-development agreements, filed by the entities themselves. Texas Open Data Portal Statewide datasets. Meetings, and how to be in the room Lubbock publishes its agendas through CivicPlus AgendaCenter : https://www.mylubbock.us/AgendaCenter Agendas are posted ahead of the meeting because the law requires it. That posting is the single most useful document in local government and almost nobody opens it — it is where a contract award, a rate change or a tax abatement appears in public for the first time, usually as one line in a consent agenda. Reading a consent agenda Items on a consent agenda are voted through together, with no discussion, in a few seconds. That is not a trick — it is how a body gets through routine business. But it means the only chance to see an item is before the meeting, in the packet. Any member can pull an item out for discussion, and so can a resident who asks one in time. Where to watch → Open the agenda portal → A link that does not work Cities move pages. Every link on this page is re-checked automatically each week and the result is published on the automation page . If one is broken and we have not caught it, tell us .

records.title: A city that owns its power company, on a shrinking aquifer
records.summary: A city that owns its power company, on a shrinking aquifer — a Move Weight Foundation chapter covering Lubbock, Lubbock County. File a records request, read the agendas, watch the meetings.
records.text: Lubbock, TX — public records and meeting archive Skip to content Why Lubbock Lubbock runs a municipal electric utility and sits on the Ogallala. Industrial load growth — including data-centre-scale load — lands on ratepayers through the utility rather than through the tax roll, which means the decision that raises a household bill is made in a utility board packet, not in a budget hearing. The Move Weight Foundation's first chapter is a town of thirteen thousand people in Ottawa County, Oklahoma, and it now holds 522 archived meetings with machine transcripts. The second is San Angelo, Texas. The third is Southaven, Mississippi, where the City's own released documents show an ad valorem agreement abating two thirds of property tax on a recital of twenty new jobs. None of those started with a tip. They started with somebody reading the agenda. If you already know something Send it anonymously . A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in metadata.

records.title: Read the people who cover this every day
records.summary: Local and statewide newsrooms covering Lubbock and Texas. We link out; we never republish another newsroom
records.text: Lubbock news & allies | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content Why we link instead of republish Local newsrooms are paid by attention. An aggregator that lifts a paragraph and keeps the reader on its own page takes that attention and gives nothing back, and then the newsroom shrinks and there is less reporting for everyone — including for us, because most of what a records request confirms was first noticed by a reporter. So the rule here is absolute: link out, never republish . The only documents hosted on this site are public records, which belong to the public already. Working on Lubbock? If you are a reporter, a nonprofit or a resident group working on something here, the archive and the request pipeline are yours to use, and we will file on your behalf if a request under your own name would cost you something. Get in touch .

records.title: File a request the city has to answer
records.summary: How to file a public records request with the City of Lubbock under Tex. Gov
records.text: File a Texas Public Information Act request in Lubbock | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content Build your letter This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere, stored, or seen by us — copy the result and send it yourself from your own email. Your name Your email What you are asking for Date range Ask for electronic delivery Require a cost estimate before charges Require an itemised legal basis for anything withheld Copy the letter Write the request narrow, then widen it “All emails about the project” gets refused as overbroad and burns your deadline. “Emails between the City Manager and [named party] between 1 March and 30 April” gets answered. Once you see what came back, ask again with what you learned. Two narrow requests beat one that never gets filled. Where to send it Lubbock's own records channel is listed on the City Desk , with the exact URL the City publishes. Use it — a request filed through the body's own portal is the hardest one for it to say it never received. Send a copy to foia@moveweight.com at the same time. We log the send date, watch the deadline, and if it lapses we publish that fact. A request nobody knows about is a request the city can ignore quietly. Track the clock § 552.301 gives the City ten (10) business days. Put the send date in your calendar with that many days added, and put a second reminder a week later. Most requests are not denied — they are simply never answered, and the only thing that changes that is somebody noticing on the exact day. If you are refused Texas has no free citizen appeal board. If the City wants to withhold, it must ask the Attorney General for a ruling within ten business days (§ 552.301) and send you a copy of what it asked — that request and the ruling are both public, and they are the best record of what a city tried to hide. If the City simply never answers, a complaint goes to the county or district attorney under § 552.3215, or you can sue for mandamus under § 552.321. Keep the refusal Whatever the outcome, keep the exact wording of the denial and the date. A refusal that cites no statute, or cites one that does not apply, is itself the story — and it is the document an appeal turns on.

It is also a way to reach the offices, portals and phone numbers you actually need — the city’s own pages, the county’s, and the Texas bodies that hear a complaint when a city will not answer. Where the full directory lives Every one of these links is on the City Desk , grouped by city government, records and transparency, Lubbock County and Texas offices, and how to be in the room at a meeting. Each is re-fetched every week, and the date it was last checked is published on the page. What you will find there City government — the council, the clerk, the departments, and the city’s own site. Records & transparency — where to file a request, where budgets and finances are published. Lubbock County and Texas — county offices, and the state bodies that oversee open records and public money. Meetings — when they happen, where the agenda is posted, and how to speak. Why we link out rather than copy The city’s own page is the authority. Our job is to make sure you can find it, and to notice when it moves or goes dark — not to stand between you and it. So every link here points at the source, and the weekly check tells you if one has stopped working. Where a page has been taken down and it mattered, we keep a dated copy and say plainly that it is a copy, with a link to the live original. Found a dead or wrong link? records.title: A city that owns its power company, on a shrinking aquifer
records.summary: The structural question this chapter was opened on, the specific public record that answers it, and what has been asked for so far.
records.text: What we are asking Lubbock | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Lubbock, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Question · Lubbock, TX A city that owns its power company, on a shrinking aquifer Lubbock runs a municipal electric utility and sits on the Ogallala. Industrial load growth — including data-centre-scale load — lands on ratepayers through the utility rather than through the tax roll, which means the decision that raises a household bill is made in a utility board packet, not in a budget hearing. This is a question, not an accusation No one at this Foundation has alleged that anybody in Lubbock has done anything wrong, and nothing on this site should be read that way. Chapters are opened on structural risk — large capital programmes, fast growth, a single dominant employer, a utility or authority that meets away from the council — because those are the conditions under which decisions get made with nobody watching. That is a statement about attention, not about anybody's conduct. Naming a city next to an accusation we have not documented would be precisely the thing this project exists to oppose. So the page you are reading names the question and the record that settles it, and then we go and ask for the record. The record that answers it Lubbock Power & Light board agendas and rate ordinances, and the City's water supply and wholesale-power contracts. How this gets resolved Ask. A request goes to the City of Lubbock under Tex. Gov't Code ch. 552. The City has ten (10) business days. Publish what comes back, whole. Released public records go up unredacted. We do not summarise a document in place of showing it, and we do not redact what the government already released. Publish what does not come back. A missed deadline, a refusal with no statute cited, an estimate that prices a resident out — those get published too, with dates. Silence is a finding. Rewrite this page. When the documents are in, this page stops being a question and becomes what the records showed — including if they showed nothing. A chapter that only ever reports wrongdoing is not doing arithmetic, it is doing marketing. What you can do right now You do not need us. The statute is yours, and a request from a resident of Lubbock is harder to wave away than one from a nonprofit two states over. Build the letter → Where to send it → Send us something anonymously →

records.title: Watch your government
records.summary: Where to watch Lubbock government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | Lubbock | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Lubbock, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Lubbock, TX Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives These are Lubbock's own recordings and portals. We link to them rather than rehosting, so you are watching the authoritative copy. Meetings — agendas and video City of Lubbock Open → City news channel (MyLBK Connect) City of Lubbock Carries Council live and every past Council meeting. Open → Council meeting video archive City of Lubbock Swagit archive of Council meetings. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet for this chapter. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.

Northwest Passage Public Improvement District
Public Hearing for the Review of the Assessment Rate
September 22, 2026 ❘ 2:00 P.M.
Citizens Tower Council Chamber ❘ 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401
Please take notice that on September 22, 2026, at 2:00 P.M., the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a
public hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose
of this hearing is to consider the 2026 assessment rate for property owners in the Northwest Passage Public
Improvement District (“District”) pursuant to Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”).
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral
objections will be considered. The Assessment Roll will be available for viewing in the Business Development
Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower after September 11, 2026.
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing:
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements are: (i) the
design, construction and maintenance of parks and greens, together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities
such as playgrounds, athletic facilities, pavilions, community facilities, bridges, walkways, lighting, benches, trash
receptacles and similar items located therein along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar infrastructure
involved in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscaping and irrigation; the design,
construction and maintenance of water features such as lakes, ponds and fountains; distinctive lighting and signs;
construction and improvement of pedestrian malls, passages or pathways including pedestrian bridges; design,
construction and improvement of vehicular bridges and low water crossings; design, construction and improvement
of community meeting halls or similar buildings; design, construction and improvement of community monuments,
towers, and other amenity-type structures; acquisition and installation of art work; design, acquisition, installation,
and improvement of telecommunication and similar technology systems; and special supplemental services defined
in the Act, together with related permits and licenses; and (ii) payment of costs associated with developing and
financing the public improvements listed in subdivision, including costs of establishing, administering and operating
the District; and (iii) the District shall prioritize its expenditures as follows: (a) design, construction, maintenance,
and financing for drainage improvements; then (b) design, construction, maintenance, and financing for park
improvements; then (c) selection, acquisition, and maintenance for public art; then (d) all other allowable
improvements and related expenditures. The District is to supplement and enhance services within the District, but
not replace or supplant existing City services provided within the District.
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The total estimated cost of services provided by the District is
estimated at $302,940 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost rises from $14,230 in FY 2026-27 to
$80,646 in FY 2030-31. The costs are based on a proposed assessment rate of $0.15 per $100.00 of valuation through
tax year 2030.
Boundaries: The District is located wholly within the City of Lubbock, Texas. The Northwest Passage Public
Improvement District (PID) generally covers a portion of an area in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas,
generally bounded by Frankford Avenue on the west, Quaker Avenue on the east, Kent Avenue and Highway 84 on
the north, and Marshall Avenue on the south. A detailed map of the District and a legal description, as well as the
Assessment Roll, is available in the Business Development Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower.
Public hearings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact
the City Secretary’s Office at 806-775-2025 or write to P.O. Box 2000, Lubbock, Texas, 79457, at least 48 hours in
advance of the public hearing.
Any questions concerning the matters described in this notice should be directed to: Molly Ballesteros, City of
Lubbock Business Development Department at 806-775-3083.

Transportation Policy Committee

Members of the public may comment on items listed on the agenda. Comments are limited to 
three minutes per speaker. 
5. 
Consider approval of the August 18, 2026, meeting minutes for the Transportation Policy 
Committee. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of the August 18, 2026, Transportation Policy Committee meeting minutes. 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approve. 
 
6. 
Take Action Regarding Office Space Procurement and Lease Negotiations 
Discussion: 
Staff will present an update on the evaluation of the current LMPO office lease and other 
available office locations. The comparison will consider usable space, services, accessibility, 
lease terms, and total occupancy cost. The Committee will consider whether to extend the 
current lease or select another location. 
 
Attachments: (Cost breakdown considering different tenants) 
 
Action Requested: Consider and take appropriate action regarding the preferred office location 
and authorize the Executive Director to negotiate and execute the related lease arrangements, 
subject to legal review, available funding, and applicable procurement requirements. 
 
Staff Recommendation: Authorize the Executive Director to proceed with the option that 
provides the best overall value and meets LMPO’s operational requirements. 

7. 
Considerations for Transportation Policy Committee Nominations 
Discussion: 
The LMPO bylaws provide for the election of a Chair and Vice Chair in October of each even 
numbered year. Nominations will be received from among the current voting members of the 
Transportation Policy Committee in preparation for the October 2026 election. 
 
Action Requested: Receive nominations for Chair and Vice Chair. No election will occur at this 
meeting. 
 
Staff Recommendation: Receive nominations, confirm eligibility under the bylaws, and conduct 
the election at the October 2026 meeting. 
 
8. 
Professional Services for Development of the Metropolitan Transportation Plan 2055 
Discussion: 
Staff will present the tentative schedule and anticipated scope of work for development of the 
MTP 2055. The Committee will consider available methods for obtaining professional services, 
including coordination with TxDOT through an available statewide consultant contract or 
conducting a separate consultant procurement. 
 
Action Requested: Consider and take appropriate action regarding the method for obtaining 
professional services and authorize staff to solicit, negotiate, and engage a qualified consultant 
for development of the MTP 2055, subject to available funding and applicable procurement 
requirements. 
 
Staff Recommendation: Authorize staff to begin the consultant selection and negotiation 
process so development of the MTP 2055 can begin during FY 2027. 
 
9. 
Fiscal True up and End of Year financial Summary Projection. 
Discussion 
Staff will present the projected Fiscal Year 2026 financial position and an update on the 
reconciliation of revenues, expenditures, reimbursements, encumbrances, and contractual 
obligations. The review will identify remaining expenses and accounting adjustments that must 
be completed before fiscal year closeout. 
 
Action Requested: 
Consider and take appropriate action regarding payment of remaining eligible Fiscal Year 2026 
obligations and completion of the accounting adjustments necessary to close the fiscal year. 
 
Staff Recommendation: Approve payment and reconciliation of eligible and properly supported 
obligations within the adopted Fiscal Year 2026 budget.

Recomendación del personal: Recibir nominaciones, confirmar la elegibilidad según los 
estatutos y llevar a cabo la elección en la reunión de octubre de 2026.

Recomendación del personal: Aprobar el pago y la conciliación de obligaciones elegibles y 
debidamente respaldadas dentro del presupuesto adoptado para el año fiscal 2026.

Council attendance column to the Electric Utility Board attendance column. Board

Officer, or his designee, regarding strategic planning, board committee reports, association
matters, ordinance change requests, EUB policy and procedures, customer service,
business center practices, procedures and policies, transition to retail customer choice,
customer concerns and complaints, billing system, forms and procedures, status of
transmission and distribution projects, generation, mutual aid, weather events, outage and
restoration efforts, grid matters, Electric Reliability Council of Texas (“ERCOT”) matters
and committee participation, staffing levels, personnel, regulatory matters, training,
cybersecurity, mutual aid agreement, and operational performance metrics.
 LP&L Chief Administrative Officer Joel Ivy discussed the governor’s announcement 
that municipal utilities should join the retail market, what the utility community thinks 
and items LP&L Chief Public Affairs Officer Matt Rose has discussed with the utility 
community regarding LP&L’s unique situation in joining the market. 
LP&L Chief Operating Officer Blair McGinnis presented information regarding the 
public comment from Jordan Wheatley. Chief McGinnis stated all costs incurred in 
electric development have increased. Chief McGinnis presented information that costs 
for transformers have increased over 100% since 2021, trenching and boring costs have 
increased up to 282% since 2022, and that these contract costs were previously approved 
by the Board. Chief McGinnis stated LP&L offered developers the ability to complete 
trenching and boring services on their own. 
Board members presented multiple questions to Chief McGinnis and Chief Ivy and 
discussed the possibility of lowering development costs. Board Member Fields asked 
LP&L staff to complete an analysis on the impact such a discount would have on LP&L’s 
revenue. Board Chair Davis asked Ex-Officio Board Member and Mayor Mark 
McBrayer if the City of Lubbock provides developers a discount or subsidy for building 
roads, sewers, and other infrastructure in developments. Mayor McBrayer stated the City 
does not provide such discounts. Chief McGinnis stated part of the difficulty is the work 
is so cost prohibitive for the majority of contractors – LP&L had only a single bidder for 
the work. 
Board Chair Davis stated Board Members Mike Stevens, Thomas Parker, and himself 
would meet with LP&L staff to discuss this topic in further detail. 
10.

audits, and financial policies of Lubbock Power & Light relating to debt issuance issues
and historical debt matters, reserve account funding, cost allocation, revenue and expense

projections, customer metering, tariff and billing, service and administrative issues, and 
risk management information including rates. 
LP&L Director of Finance Kasey Johnson discussed the balance sheet and cash flows 
for June 2026. Director Johnson also discussed financial ratios, LP&L’s June income 
statement, and current budget to actual comparisons. 
11.
Discuss and take action to amend the Fiscal Year 2026-27 System Delivery Rate/Tariff
Schedule and make appropriate recommendations to the City Council of the City of
Lubbock pursuant to §2.03.415(a) of the Code of Ordinances, City of Lubbock, Texas.
Board Member Dr. Craig Rhyne discussed the August 11, 2026 Financial Review
Committee Meeting that also presented this same information.
LP&L Director of Financial Planning and Analysis Daniel Garcia provided a recap and
review of the cost of service analysis. Director Garcia stated there is great pressure to
increase electric distribution rates but LP&L can offset with reserves to help customers
keep costs low. Director Garcia discussed usage trends, delivery rate comparisons, and
LP&L rate benchmarking.
Board Secretary Gwen Stafford made a motion to approve the rate schedule, which was
seconded by Board Member Rhyne. The Board approved the motion by a vote of 9-0.
12.
Discuss and take possible minuted action regarding the location of the regular scheduled
Board meeting for October 20, 2026.
Chief Ivy discussed moving the October EUB meeting to the Lubbock Civic Center to
celebrate Board Secretary Stafford’s last meeting and years of service on behalf of
LP&L. A motion to approve moving the October meeting was made by Board Member
Stevens, which was seconded by Board Member Rhyne. The Board approved the
motion by a vote of 9-0

6.

del Comité Asesor de Transporte celebrada el 13 de agosto de 2026. 
Recomendación del personal: Aprobar. 
7. 
Considerar las nominaciones para los cargos de Presidente y Vicepresidente del 
Comité Asesor de Transporte.

Vicepresidente del Comité Asesor de Transporte. 

Recomendación del personal: Celebrar la votación durante la reunión de octubre 
del Comité Asesor de Transporte.

elaboración del contrato de arrendamiento de la LMPO y presentará un desglose de 
los servicios admisibles que se proporcionarán. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar de los hallazgos 
al Comité de Política de Transporte, según corresponda. 
Recomendación del personal: Remitir la información sobre el contrato de 
arrendamiento al Comité de Política de Transporte.

Plan de Transporte Metropolitano 2055.

opciones para anunciar la solicitud y contratar a un consultor que actualice el Plan 
de Transporte Metropolitano. 
Acción solicitada: Discutir y tomar acción para coordinar con TxDOT la 
actualización del MTP mediante el consultor estatal con contrato de servicios a 
demanda (on-call).

realizar la actualización del MTP mediante el consultor estatal con contrato de 
servicios a demanda.

Recibir una actualización sobre los Créditos para el Desarrollo del Transporte

proceder el personal de la LMPO y el Comité Asesor de Transporte.

Discusión: El personal informará al Comité Asesor de Transporte sobre la 
clasiﬁcación funcional de las vialidades evaluadas dentro del área de planiﬁcación

consultor para presentarlas al CAT. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar de los hallazgos 
al Comité de Política de Transporte, según corresponda.

Informes:

o Citibus 
o LPD/DPS 
o Texas Tech University 
o Presentación del Subcomité de Transporte de la LMPO

Clausura de la sesión.

Members of the public may comment on items listed on the agenda. Comments are limited

5. 
Consider approval of the June 16, 2026, meeting minutes for the Transportation 
Policy Committee. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of the June 16, 2026, Transportation Policy Committee 
meeting minutes. 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approve. 
6. 
TxDOT Freight Industry Workshop. 
Discussion: 
Staff will provide an overview of the Freight Industry Workshop to be conducted here in 
the Lubbock County building by TxDOT and WSP. Attendance will consist of freight 
industry representatives operating in and around the greater Lubbock area, local 
officials, economic development partners, and additional stakeholders across the region. 
 
Action Requested: No action required 
 
Staff Recommendation: No recommendation 
 
7. 
Provide an update to the Transportation Policy Committee on discussions 
focused on non-federalized funding mechanisms for establishing a predictable 
annual local contribution for grant matching and project development. 
Discussion: 
Staff will provide an update on how other governmental entities have established local 
funding mechanisms to support grant match requirements, project development, and 
other non-federal funding needs. The discussion will include previously discussed 
funding sources and how other governmental agencies utilize these funds. 
 
Action Requested: 

Make a recommendation to continue to evaluate other non-federalized funding 
opportunities. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Continue the evaluation process and present the findings to the Transportation Policy 
Committee. 
 
8. 
FY 2027-2028 Unified Planning Work Program Revenue Amendment. 
Discussion 
This proposed amendment to the FY 2027–2028 Unified Planning Work Program 
reconciles projected revenues with the latest formula funding estimates provided by 
TxDOT. These revised numbers reflect a lower than anticipated revenue stream due to 
the lack of a new federal transportation bill and current economic conditions, which have 
idropped funding below the amounts used in the original UPWP submission. Staff will 
present these updated available planning funds to align the budget with the new financial 
realities. 
 
Action Requested: 
Consider approval of the proposed FY 2027-2028 UPWP amendment. 
 
Staff Recommendation: Approve 
9. 
FY 2025-2026 Unified Planning Work Program (UPWP) Benefit Cost Analysis 
Amendment 
 
Discussion 
Discuss and take action on an amendment to the FY 2025–2026 Unified Planning Work 
Program (UPWP) to add a Benefit-Cost Analysis (BCA) to Subtask 3.1.A. The LMPO 
partnered with TxDOT to utilize TxDOT on-call consultant to prepare the required BCA—
consisting of both a draft workbook and a narrative—for the Infrastructure for Rebuilding 
America (INFRA) grant application for Loop 88 Segments 3F and 3G. This amendment 
reallocates funding to support completion of the BCA, which is a U.S. Department of 
Transportation requirement and provides a quantitative assessment of project benefits 
relative to costs. 
 
Action Requested: 
Consider approval of an amendment to the FY2025 – 2026 Unified Planning Work 
Program 
 
Staff Recommendation: Approve 
 
10. 
Reports: 
• 
LMPO’s 
o Subcommittee on Transportation Funding Testimony Invitation 
o NADO 2026 Excellence in Regional Transportation Award and 
Conference Report

Lubbock, Texas 79401

Reconocimiento del Quórum

Comentarios y agradecimientos públicos a los invitados

5. 
Considere la aprobación del acta de la reunión del 16 de junio de 2026 para el 
Comité de Política de Transporte. 
Acción requerida: 
Considerar la aprobación de las actas de la reunión del Comité de Política de 
Transporte del 16 de junio de 2026. 
Recomendación del personal: 
 Aprobar. 
6. 
Taller de la industria de mercancías de TxDOT. 
Discusión: 
El personal ofrecerá una visión general del Taller de la Industria de Mercancías que se 
llevará a cabo aquí en el edificio del condado de Lubbock por TxDOT y WSP. La 
asistencia estará compuesta por representantes de la industria de mercancías que 
operen en y alrededor del área metropolitana de Lubbock, funcionarios locales, socios 
para el desarrollo económico y otros actores de toda la región. 
 
Acción solicitada: No se requiere ninguna acción 
 
Recomendación del personal: Sin recomendación 
 
7. 
Proporcionar una actualización al Comité de Política de Transporte sobre las 
discusiones centradas en mecanismos de financiación no federalizados para 
establecer una contribución anual local previsible para la igualación de 
subvenciones y el desarrollo de proyectos. 
Discusión: 
El personal proporcionará una actualización sobre cómo otras entidades 
gubernamentales han establecido mecanismos locales de financiación para apoyar los 
requisitos de igualación de subvenciones, el desarrollo de proyectos y otras 

necesidades de financiación no federales. La discusión incluirá fuentes de financiación 
previamente discutidas y cómo otras agencias gubernamentales utilizan estos fondos. 
 
Acción solicitada: 
Haz una recomendación para seguir evaluando otras oportunidades de financiación no 
federalizadas. 
 
Recomendación del personal: 
Continúa el proceso de evaluación y presenta los resultados al Comité de Política de 
Transporte. 
 
8. 
Enmienda de Ingresos del Programa Unificado de Trabajo de Planificación del año 
fiscal 2027-2028. 
Discusión 
Esta enmienda propuesta al Programa Unificado de Trabajo de Planificación del año 
fiscal 2027–2028 concilia los ingresos proyectados con las últimas estimaciones de 
financiación por fórmula proporcionadas por TxDOT. Estas cifras revisadas reflejan una 
fuente de ingresos inferior a la prevista debido a la falta de un nuevo proyecto federal de 
ley de transporte y a las condiciones económicas actuales, que han ireducido la 
financiación por debajo de las cantidades utilizadas en la presentación original del 
UPWP. El personal presentará estos fondos de planificación actualizados disponibles 
para alinear el presupuesto con las nuevas realidades financieras. 
 
Acción solicitada: 
Considere la aprobación de la enmienda propuesta del UPWP para el año fiscal 2027-
2028. 
 
Recomendación del personal: Aprobar 
9. 
Enmienda de Análisis de Costes de Beneficios del Programa Unificado de Trabajo 
de Planificación (UPWP) para el año fiscal 2025-2026 
 
Discusión 
Debatir y tomar medidas sobre una enmienda al Programa Unificado de Trabajo de 
Planificación (UPWP) para el año fiscal 2025–2026 para añadir un Análisis de Coste de 
Beneficios (BCA) a la Subtarea 3.1.A. La LMPO se asoció con TxDOT para utilizar al 
consultor de guardia de TxDOT para preparar el BCA requerido —que consiste tanto en 
un borrador de cuaderno de trabajo como en una narración— para la solicitud de 
subvención Infrastructure for Rebuilding America (INFRA) para los segmentos 3F y 3G 
del Loop 88. Esta enmienda reasigna fondos para apoyar la finalización del BCA, que es 
un requisito del Departamento de Transporte de EE. UU. y proporciona una evaluación 
cuantitativa de los beneficios del proyecto en relación con los costes. 
 
Acción solicitada: 
Considere la aprobación de una enmienda al Programa Unificado de Trabajo de 
Planificación para el año fiscal 2025 – 2026

5. 
FY 2027-2028 Unified Planning Work Program (UPWP) Revenue Amendment. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
This proposed amendment to the FY 2027–2028 Unified Planning Work Program 
reconciles projected revenues with the latest formula funding estimates provided 
by TxDOT. These revised numbers reflect a lower than anticipated revenue 
stream due to the lack of a new federal transportation bill and current economic 
conditions, which dropped funding below the amounts used in the original UPWP 
submission. Staff will present these updated available planning funds to align the 
budget with the new financial realities. 
 
Action Requested: A Consider recommendation of the proposed FY 2027-2028 
UPWP amendment to the Transportation Policy Committee. 
 
6. 
FY 2025-2026 Unified Planning Work Program (UPWP) Benefit Cost Analysis 
Amendment. 
 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
This proposed amendment to the 2025-2026 Unified Planning Work Program 
(UPWP) reallocates funding designated for the benefit-cost analysis of the 
Infrastructure for Rebuilding America (INFRA) program. The benefit cost analysis 
is a requirement established by the United States Department of Transportation 
(USDOT) and is essential for submitting a comprehensive application. This 
analysis quantitatively assesses the benefits that the project will deliver in 
relation to its overall costs. 
 
Action Requested: A Consider recommendation of the FY 2025-2026 UPWP 
amendment to the Transportation Policy Committee.

Esta enmienda propuesta al Programa Unificado de Trabajo de Planificación del año 
fiscal 2027–2028 concilia los ingresos proyectados con las últimas estimaciones de 
financiación por fórmula proporcionadas por TxDOT. Estas cifras revisadas reflejan una 
fuente de ingresos inferior a la prevista debido a la falta de una nueva ley federal de 
transporte y a las condiciones económicas actuales, que redujeron la financiación por 
debajo de las cantidades utilizadas en la presentación original del UPWP. El personal 
presentará estos fondos de planificación actualizados disponibles para alinear el 
presupuesto con las nuevas realidades financieras.

UPWP para el año fiscal 2027-2028 al Comité de Política de Transporte.

Planificación (UPWP) para el año fiscal 2025-2026.

(UPWP) reasigna fondos destinados al análisis de costes y beneficios del programa 
Infraestructura para Reconstruir América (INFRA). El análisis de coste de beneficio es 
un requisito establecido por el Departamento de Transporte de los Estados Unidos 
(USDOT) y es esencial para presentar una solicitud completa. Este análisis evalúa 
cuantitativamente los beneficios que el proyecto aportará en relación con sus costes

Willow Bend Villas Public Improvement District
Public Hearing for the Review of the Assessment Rate
August 11, 2026 ❘ 2:00 P.M.
Citizens Tower Council Chamber ❘ 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401
Please take notice that on August 11, 2026, at 2:00 P.M., the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a public
hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose of this
hearing is to consider the 2026 assessment rate for property owners in the Willow Bend Villas Public Improvement
District (“District”) pursuant to Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”).
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral
objections will be considered. The Assessment Roll will be available for viewing in the Business Development
Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower after July 31, 2026.
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing:
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements are: (i)
acquisition, construction, or drainage facilities or improvements, (ii) the design, construction and maintenance of
parks and green spaces, together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities such as playgrounds, splash pads,
pool(s), athletic facilities, pavilions, community facilities, irrigation, walkways, lighting, benches, trash receptacles
and any similar items located there in along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar infrastructure involved
in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscaping and irrigation; and (iii) payment of costs
associated with developing and financing the public improvements listed in subdivision (iv) including costs of
establishing, administering and operating the District. The District is to supplement and enhance services within the
District, but not replace or supplant existing City services provided within the District.
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The total estimated cost of services provided by the District is
estimated at $773,731 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost changes from $148,679 in FY 2026-27 to
$160,935 in FY 2030-31. The District shall not incur bonded indebtedness. The costs are based on a proposed
assessment rate of $0.22 per $100.00 of valuation through tax year 2030.
Boundaries: The District is located wholly within the City of Lubbock, Texas. The Willow Bend Villas Public
Improvement District covers a portion of an area in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas, generally bounded
by 19th Street to the north, the alley between Kelsey Avenue and Kenwood Avenue to the east, and railroad tracks to
the south and west. A detailed map of the District and a legal description, as well as the Assessment Roll, is available
in the Business Development Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower.
Public hearings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact
the City Secretary’s Office at 806-775-2025 or write to P.O. Box 2000, Lubbock, Texas, 79457, at least 48 hours in
advance of the public hearing.
Any questions concerning the matters described in this notice should be directed to: Danielle Williams, City of
Lubbock Business Development Department at 806-775-3082.

Quincy Park Public Improvement District
Public Hearing for the Review of the Assessment Rate
August 11, 2026 ❘ 2:00 P.M.
Citizens Tower Council Chamber ❘ 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401
Please take notice that on August 11, 2026, at 2:00 P.M., the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a public
hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose of this
hearing is to consider the 2026 assessment rate for property owners in the Quincy Park Public Improvement District
(“District”) pursuant to Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”).
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral
objections will be considered. The Assessment Roll will be available for viewing in the Business Development
Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower after July 31, 2026.
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing:
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements are: (i) the
design, construction and maintenance of Parks and greens together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities
such as playgrounds, athletic facilities, pavilions, community facilities, irrigation, walkways, lighting, benches, trash
receptacles and any similar items located therein along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar infrastructure
involved in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscape and irrigation; and (ii) payment of
costs associated with developing and financing the public improvements listed in subdivision (i) including costs of
establishing, administering and operating the District. The District is to supplement and enhance services within the
District, but not replace or supplant existing City services provided within the District.
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The total estimated cost of services provided by the District is
estimated at $891,870 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost changes from $192,557 in FY 2026-27 to
$179,308 in FY 2030-31. The District shall not incur bonded indebtedness. The costs are based on a proposed
assessment rate of $0.14 per $100.00 of valuation through tax year 2030.
Boundaries: The District is located wholly within the City of Lubbock, Texas. The Quincy Park Public Improvement
District generally covers an area bounded by portions of 88th and 89th Street on the north, Upland Avenue on the
west, 98th Street on the south, and Quincy Avenue on the east. A detailed map of the District and a legal description,
as well as the Assessment Roll, is available in the Business Development Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens
Tower.
Public hearings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact
the City Secretary’s Office at 806-775-2025 or write to P.O. Box 2000, Lubbock, Texas, 79457, at least 48 hours in
advance of the public hearing.
Any questions concerning the matters described in this notice should be directed to: Danielle Williams, City of
Lubbock Business Development Department at 806-775-3082.

Committee Chair Dr. Craig Rhyne called the meeting to order at 11:02 a.m.
2.
Public Comment. Public comment is an opportunity for the public to make comments and
express a position on agenda items.
a.
This period, of up to thirty minutes, is dedicated to public comment. Each member of the
public will have three minutes to speak. Any member of the public that requires assistance
of a translator will have six minutes to speak. Comments must be limited to only those
items posted on the Financial Review Committee /EUB agenda. Any member of the public
wishing to speak shall sign up on the public comment sheet on the day of the Financial
Review Committee /EUB meeting. The Financial Review Committee /EUB shall follow
the order of people wishing to speak as listed on the sign-up sheet. If everyone who signed
up to speak has been given an opportunity to speak and the thirty minutes designated for
public comment has not been exhausted, the Financial Review Committee /EUB may, at

its discretion, open the floor to anyone else wishing to address the Financial Review 
Committee /EUB, subject to all the same procedures and guidelines.

3. Approve the minutes from the last Financial Review Committee meeting held on February
11, 2026.
A motion to approve the minutes from the February 11, 2026 meeting was made by Board
Secretary Gwen Stafford, which was seconded by Board Vice Chair Eddie Schulz. The
motion was passed 4-0.

but not limited, to revenue and expense projections, tariff and billing, service and
administrative issues, including risk management information and rates and strategic plan,
borrowing related to transmission projects, and proceeds from generation sale.
LP&L Chief Financial Officer Harvey Hall introduced the financial team involved in
drafting the 2026-27 budget: Daniel Garcia, Erich Von Heuval, Ricky Rodriguez, Joel Ivy,
and Harvey Hall. Chief Hall presented the strategic plan update including updates on the
Department of Energy, rates, LP&L’s cash position, and proposed budget options. Chief
Hall also discussed LP&L’s future plans for customer value, financial resiliency, and
system modernization.
LP&L Director of Financial Planning & Analysis Daniel Garcia thanked Ricky Rodriguez
for his hard work and recent transition on the financial team. Director Garcia then
presented the 2026-27 proposed budget including: budget highlights, year-over-year
expense comparisons, funding sources and revenues, projected expenses for 2026-27,
capital program overview, and budget timeline. Secretary Stafford questioned Director
Garcia about expenses LP&L transfers to the City of Lubbock; Director Garcia stated the
total transfers to the City in 2026-27 will be $20.2 million – this includes $1.2 million credit
LP&L is giving to the City through LP&L delaying collecting said amount from the City
for credit card fee reimbursement.

Please take notice that on August 26, 2025, at 2:00 P.M., the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a public
hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose of this
hearing is to consider the 2025 assessment rate for property owners in the Cypress Ranch Public Improvement District
(“District”) pursuant to Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”).
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral
objections will be considered. The Assessment roll will be available for viewing in the City Secretary’s Office after
August 15,2025.
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing:
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements are: (i)
acquisition, construction, or drainage facilities or improvements, the design, construction, and maintenance of parks
and green spaces, together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities such as playgrounds, splash pads,
pool(s), receptacles and any similar items located there in along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar
infrastructure involved in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscaping and irrigation; and
(ii) payment of costs associated with developing and financing the public improvements listed in subdivision,
including costs of establishing, administering and operating the District. The District is to supplement and enhance
services within the District, but not replace or supplant existing City services provided within the District.
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The total estimated cost of services provided by the District
is estimated at $293,048 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost rises from $14,850 in FY 2025-26 to
$82,560 in FY 2029-30. The District shall not incur bonded indebtedness. The costs are based on a proposed
assessment rate of $0.15 per $100.00 of valuation through tax year 2029.
Boundaries: The District is located within the City of Lubbock, Texas. The proposed Cypress Ranch Public
Improvement District (PID) generally covers a portion of an area in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas,
generally bounded by the Levelland Highway to the north, agricultural land to the east, railroad tracks to the south,
and Inler Avenue to the west. A detailed map of the District and a legal description as well as the Assessment Roll
is available in the Business Development Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower.

advance of the public hearing.

Lubbock Business Development Department at 775-3082.

Transportation Advisory Committee 
August 6, 2026, 10:00 a.m. 
916 Main Street, 1st Floor Bank Lobby 
Lubbock, Texas 79401 
 
1. 
Call to Order of the Transportation Advisory Committee 
2. 
Acknowledgment of Quorum 
3. 
Safety Procedures 
4. 
Public Comment and Acknowledgment of Guests 
Members of the public may comment on items listed on the agenda. Comments are limited 
to three minutes per speaker. 
5. 
Consider approval of the July 9, 2026, meeting minutes for the Transportation Advisory 
Committee. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of the July 9, 2026, Transportation Advisory Committee meeting 
minutes. 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approve. 
 
6. 
TxDOT Freight Industry Workshop 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide an overview of the Freight Industry Workshop to be conducted here in 
the Lubbock County building by TxDOT and WSP. Attendance will consist of freight 
industry representatives operating in and around the greater Lubbock area, local 
officials, economic development partners, and additional stakeholders across the region. 

Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
7. 
Discuss funding mechanisms for establishing a predictable annual local 
contribution for grant matching and project development. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 

Staff will provide an update on how other governmental entities have established local 
funding mechanisms to support grant match requirements, project development, and 
other non-federal funding needs. The discussion will include previously discussed 
funding sources and how other governmental agencies utilize these funds. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
8. 
Receive an update regarding MPO Office Space and Lease Status 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
The LMPO’s current office lease expires September 30, 2026. Staff will report on the 
review of available office space, including the existing location, other public facilities, and 
private market alternatives. The report will also address lease timing, operational needs, 
public accessibility, parking, technology requirements, and the status of any discussions 
authorized by the Transportation Policy Committee. 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
9. 
Follow up and discussion regarding the Draft Metropolitan Transportation Plan Project 
List. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will continue the review of the draft Metropolitan Transportation Plan project list and 
provide additional information requested by the Committee. The review is intended to 
confirm that listed projects remain current, reflect documented regional transportation 
needs, and are appropriately classified within the Metropolitan Transportation Plan. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
10. 
FY 2027-2028 Unified Planning Work Program Revenue Amendment. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
This proposed amendment to the FY 2027–2028 Unified Planning Work Program 
reconciles projected revenues with the latest formula funding estimates provided 
by TxDOT. These revised numbers reflect a lower than anticipated revenue 
stream due to the lack of a new federal transportation bill and current economic 
conditions, which dropped funding below the amounts used in the original UPWP 
submission. Staff will present these updated available planning funds to align the 
budget with the new financial realities. 
 
Action Requested: A Consider recommendation of the proposed FY 2027-2028 
UPWP amendment to the Transportation Policy Committee. 

11. 
NADO 2026 Excellence in Regional Transportation Award and Conference Report 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
The South Plains Regional Commuter Mobility and Transit Demand Study has 
been selected for a 2026 Excellence in Regional Transportation Award by the 
NADO Research Foundation and RPO America. Developed by the South Plains 
Association of Governments alongside local partners, regional transit providers, 
TxDOT, and the Lubbock Metropolitan Planning Organization, this study 
functions as a high-level screening tool to isolate future transit corridors. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 

12. 
Reports: 
• 
TxDOT 
• 
Citibus 
• 
LPD/DPS 
• 
Texas Tech University 
• 
LMPO’s 
 
13. 
Adjourn 

Comité Asesor de Transporte 
Agosto 6, 2026, 10:00 a.m. 
916 Main Street, 1ª planta Vestíbulo del Banco 
Lubbock, Texas 79401 
 
1. 
Convocatoria al Orden del Comité Asesor de Transporte 
2. 
Reconocimiento del Quórum 
3. 
Procedimientos de seguridad 
4. 
Comentarios y agradecimientos públicos a los invitados 
El público puede comentar los puntos listados en la agenda. Los comentarios están 
limitados a tres minutos por ponente. 
5. 
Considere la aprobación del acta de la reunión del Julio 9, 2026 para el Comité Asesor de 
Transporte. 
Acción requerida: 
Considerar la aprobación de las actas de la reunión del Comité Asesor de Transporte 
del 9 de julio de 2026. 
Recomendación del personal: 
 Aprobar. 
 
6. 
Taller de la Industria de Mercancías de TxDOT 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El personal ofrecerá una visión general del Taller de la Industria de Mercancías que se 
llevará a cabo aquí en el edificio del condado de Lubbock por TxDOT y WSP. La 
asistencia estará compuesta por representantes de la industria de mercancías que 
operen en y alrededor del área metropolitana de Lubbock, funcionarios locales, socios 
para el desarrollo económico y otros actores de toda la región. 

Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No hace falta ninguna acción. Informa de las 
conclusiones al Comité de Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
 
7. 
Debatir los mecanismos de financiación para establecer una contribución local 
anual previsible para la igualación de subvenciones y el desarrollo de proyectos. 

Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El personal proporcionará una actualización sobre cómo otras entidades 
gubernamentales han establecido mecanismos locales de financiación para apoyar los 
requisitos de igualación de subvenciones, el desarrollo de proyectos y otras 
necesidades de financiación no federales. La discusión incluirá fuentes de financiación 
previamente discutidas y cómo otras agencias gubernamentales utilizan estos fondos. 
 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No hace falta ninguna acción. Informa de las 
conclusiones al Comité de Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
 
8. 
Recibe una actualización sobre el estado del espacio de oficina y el contrato de alquiler 
de MPO 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El contrato actual de la oficina de la LMPO expira el 30 de septiembre de 2026. El 
personal informará sobre la revisión de los espacios de oficinas disponibles, incluyendo 
la ubicación existente, otras instalaciones públicas y alternativas al mercado privado. El 
informe también abordará el calendario del contrato de arrendamiento, las necesidades 
operativas, la accesibilidad pública, el aparcamiento, los requisitos tecnológicos y el 
estado de cualquier discusión autorizada por el Comité de Política de Transporte. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No hace falta ninguna acción. Informa de las 
conclusiones al Comité de Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
9. 
Seguimiento y discusión sobre la Lista de Proyectos del Plan Metropolitano de 
Transporte. 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El personal continuará revisando el borrador de la lista de proyectos del Plan 
Metropolitano de Transporte y proporcionará información adicional solicitada por el 
Comité. La revisión tiene como objetivo confirmar que los proyectos listados siguen 
vigentes, reflejan las necesidades regionales de transporte documentadas y están 
debidamente clasificados dentro del Plan Metropolitano de Transporte. 
 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No hace falta ninguna acción. Informa de las 
conclusiones al Comité de Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
 
10. 
Enmienda de Ingresos del Programa Unificado de Trabajo de Planificación del año fiscal 
2027-2028. 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
Esta enmienda propuesta al Programa Unificado de Trabajo de Planificación del 
año fiscal 2027–2028 concilia los ingresos proyectados con las últimas 
estimaciones de financiación por fórmula proporcionadas por TxDOT. Estas 
cifras revisadas reflejan una fuente de ingresos inferior a la prevista debido a la 

falta de una nueva ley federal de transporte y a las condiciones económicas 
actuales, que redujeron la financiación por debajo de las cantidades utilizadas en 
la presentación original del UPWP. El personal presentará estos fondos de 
planificación actualizados disponibles para alinear el presupuesto con las nuevas 
realidades financieras. 
 
Se solicita acción: A Considerar la recomendación de la enmienda propuesta del 
UPWP para el año fiscal 2027-2028 al Comité de Política de Transporte. 
 
11. 
Premio NADO 2026 a la Excelencia en Transporte Regional e Informe de la 
Conferencia 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El Estudio de Movilidad Regional de Desplazamiento y Demanda de Transporte 
Público de South Plains ha sido seleccionado para un Premio a la Excelencia en 
Transporte Regional 2026 por la Fundación de Investigación NADO y RPO 
America. Desarrollado por la Asociación de Gobiernos de South Plains junto con 
socios locales, proveedores regionales de transporte, TxDOT y la Lubbock 
Metropolitan Planning Organization, este estudio funciona como una herramienta 
de selección de alto nivel para aislar futuros corredores de transporte. 
 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No hace falta ninguna acción. Informa de las 
conclusiones al Comité de Política de Transporte según corresponda. 

12. 
Informes: 
• 
TxDOT 
• 
Citibus 
• 
LPD/DPS 
• 
Universidad Tecnológica de Texas 
• 
LMPO's 
 
13. 
Levantamiento de la sesión

records.text:
Notice of Public Hearing for the Review of the Assessment Rate for the 
Centerpointe Public Improvement District
Please take notice that on July 28, 2026, at 2:00 P.M., the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a public
hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose of this
hearing is to consider the 2026 assessment rate for property owners in the Centerpointe Public Improvement District
(“District”) pursuant to Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”).
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral
objections will be considered. The Assessment roll will be available for viewing in the City Secretary’s Office after
July 1, 2026.
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing:
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements is: (i)
acquisition, construction, or drainage facilities or improvements, the design, construction, and maintenance of parks
and green spaces, together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities such as playgrounds, splash pads,
pool(s), receptacles and any similar items located there in along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar
infrastructure involved in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscaping and irrigation; and
(ii) payment of costs associated with developing and financing the public improvements listed in subdivision,
including costs of establishing, administering and operating the District. The District is to supplement and enhance
services within the District, but not replace or supplant existing City services provided within the District.
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The total estimated cost of services provided by the District
is estimated at $168,534 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost rises from $0 in FY 2026-27 to $72,320 in
FY 2030-31. The District shall not incur bonded indebtedness. The costs are based on a proposed assessment rate of
$0.17 per $100.00 of valuation through tax year 2030.
Boundaries: The District is located within the City of Lubbock, Texas. The proposed Centerpointe Public
Improvement District (PID) generally covers a portion of an area in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas,
generally bounded on the east by North Avenue U, on the south by Drake Street, on the west by North University,
and on the north by Georgetown Street. A detailed map of the District and a legal description as well as the
Assessment Roll is available in the Business Development Department on the 9th Floor of Citizens Tower.
Public hearings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact
the City Secretary’s Office at 775-2025 or write to P.O. Box 2000, Lubbock, Texas, 79457, at least 48 hours in
advance of the public hearing.
Any questions concerning the matters described in this notice should be directed to: Molly Ballesteros, City of
Lubbock Special Districts Manager at 775-3083.

presentations, as well as a tour of the Massingale and Yellow House facilities.

Chief Ivy reminded the Board that voting on LP&L’s budget would occur during the
July meeting and then introduced LP&L staff members Colby Morris and Paul
Koberlein for the ERCOT summer readiness program presentation. Morris and
Koberlein presented the ERCOT capacity reserves plan summary information for 2025
compared with 2026, discussed the energy emergency alert system and threshold of
alerts, and ERCOT ancillary services report – a free and publicly available resource that
contains live generation data updates. Morris and Koberlein confirmed engineering is
not concerned about ERCOT’s summer readiness.

risk management information including rates.
LP&L Director of Finance Kacey Johnson presented the balance sheet and cash flows
for April 2026. Director Johnson indicated the lower cash flow was due to lower billing
in March, which matches historical data. Director Johnson reviewed financial ratios
and LP&L’s income statement.

EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE 
OF THE 
ELECTRIC UTILITY BOARD 
AGENDA 
July 13, 2026 
12:00pm 
 
OPEN/EXECUTIVE SESSION: 
CITIZENS TOWER 
1314 Avenue K 
Lubbock, Texas 79401 
5th Floor Conference Room 501A 

1. 
Call to order. 
 
Open Session. 
 
2. 
Discuss July proposed agenda as attached which may include discussions on the 
listed agenda items. 

Executive Session 
 
3. 
Discuss July proposed agenda as attached which may include discussions on the 
following executive session items on the agenda: 
 
Hold an executive session in accordance with V.T.C.A. Government Code § 551.086, 
§552.133, and §552.1331 to discuss and deliberate, on the following competitive matters 
of Lubbock Power & Light, reasonably related to the following categories: 
 
(i) Discussion and deliberation of generation matters, including but not limited to 
generation unit and/or portfolio sale opportunities including the potential for unused 
land designated for other uses; 
 
(ii) Discussion regarding real estate purchase and transactions for future substation 
developments; 
 
(iii) Discussion of risk management, contracts, and strategies, customer billing, and usage 
information, system load characteristics, and ERCOT power analyses and strategies; 
 
(iv) Plans, studies, proposals, and analyses for system improvements, additions, or sales 
(other than transmission and distribution system improvements inside the service area 
for which the public power utility is the sole certificated retail provider); 
 
(v) info collected as part of an advanced metering system for usage, services, and billing, 
including amounts billed or collected for utility usage 

4. 
Hold an executive session in accordance with V.T.C.A. Government Code § 
551.071, seeking the advice of legal counsel about pending or contemplated 
litigation or settlement offers and hold a consultation with the attorney on matters 
in which the duty of the attorney to the Electric Utility Board under the Texas 
Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas conflicts with 
Chapter 551 of the Texas Government Code: 
 
(i) 
legal advice regarding issues herein listed on the agenda;

legal advice and counsel regarding contemplated litigation matters; 
(iii) 
legal advice and counsel regarding North American Electric Reliability 
Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection (NERC CIP) standards; 
 
(iv)

Hold an executive session in accordance with V.T.C.A. Government Code § 
551.072, to deliberate the purchase, exchange, lease, and value of real property. 
 
6. 
Hold an executive session in accordance with V.T.C.A. Government Code § 
551.074(a)(1) to deliberate the appointment and/or reappointment of a public 
officer or employee (Electric Utility Board). 
 
7. 
Hold an executive session in accordance with V.T.C.A. Government Code § 
551.074(a)(1) to deliberate the appointment, employment, evaluation, and duties of

Officer). 
 
8. 
Adjourn.

Transportation Advisory Committee 
July 9, 2026, 10:00 a.m. 
916 Main Street, 2nd Floor Conference Room 
Lubbock, Texas 79401 
 
1. 
Call to Order of the Transportation Advisory Committee 
2. 
Acknowledgment of Quorum 
3. 
Safety Procedures 
4. 
Public Comment and Acknowledgment of Guests 
Members of the public may comment on items listed on the agenda. Comments are limited 
to three minutes per speaker. 
5. 
Consider approval of the June 4, 2026, meeting minutes for the Transportation Advisory 
Committee. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of the June 4, 2026, Transportation Advisory Committee meeting 
minutes. 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approve. 
 
6. 
Receive notice regarding the National Association of Development Organizations 
(NADO) Excellence Award. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide information regarding the NADO Research Foundation Excellence 
Award for the South Plains Association of Governments South Plains Regional 
Commuter Mobility and Transit Demand Study. The award is scheduled to be recognized 
at the 2026 NADO conference. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
7. 
Discuss the Waco model as a potential framework for establishing a predictable annual 
local contribution for grant matching and project development. 

Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide a case study review of how other governmental entities have 
established local funding mechanisms to support grant match requirements, project 
development, and other non-federal funding needs. The discussion will include the Waco 
model and other comparable approaches that may assist the MPO in evaluating a 
predictable annual local contribution framework. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
8. 
Receive an update regarding office space procurement and lease negotiation authority. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide an update on the current MPO office lease, expiration timing, and the 
need to evaluate available public and private space options for continued MPO 
operations. The discussion will include the status of procurement and lease negotiation 
authority previously discussed by the Transportation Policy Committee. 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
9. 
Follow up and discussion regarding the DRAFT Metropolitan Transportation Program 
(MTP) full project list. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide additional information regarding the Draft Metropolitan Transportation 
Plan project list. MTP project lists are reviewed periodically to ensure that listed projects 
remain current, reflect regional transportation needs, and remain consistent with 
applicable TxDOT and federal planning requirements. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
10. 
Reports: 
• 
TxDOT 
• 
Citibus 
1. Update regarding 10CR Fund Transfer 
• 
LPD/DPS 
• 
Texas Tech University 
• 
LMPO’s 
1. MPO, Fiscal Agent, and TxDOT Contract 
2. Grant Pursuits 
11. 
Adjourn 

Comité Asesor de Transporte 
Julio 9, 2026, 10:00 a. m. 
916 Main Street, Sala de Conferencias, 2nd Floor 
Lubbock, Texas 79401 
1. Llamada al orden del Comité Asesor de Transporte 
2. Confirmación del quórum 
3. Procedimientos de seguridad 
4. Comentarios del público y reconocimiento de invitados 
Los miembros del público pueden comentar sobre los temas incluidos en la agenda. Los 
comentarios están limitados a tres minutos por orador. 
5. Considerar la aprobación de las actas de la reunión del Junio 4, 2026 del Comité Asesor de 
Transporte. 
Acción requerida: 
Considerar la aprobación de las actas de la reunión del 4 de junio de 2026 del Comité Asesor 
de Transporte. 
Recomendación del personal: 
Aprobar. 
6. Recibir aviso sobre el Premio a la Excelencia de la Asociación Nacional de Organizaciones de 
Desarrollo (NADO). 
Discusión y recomendación: 
El personal proporcionará información sobre el Premio a la Excelencia de la Fundación de 
Investigación de NADO otorgado al Estudio de Movilidad de Viajeros y Demanda de Tránsito 
de la Región de los Llanos del Sur de la Asociación de Gobiernos de los Llanos del Sur. El 
premio será reconocido en la conferencia NADO 2026. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar los hallazgos al Comité de 
Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
7. Analizar el modelo de Waco como un posible marco para establecer una contribución local 
anual predecible para la combinación de subvenciones y el desarrollo de proyectos. 
Discusión y recomendación: 
El personal proporcionará un análisis de caso sobre cómo otras entidades gubernamentales 
han establecido mecanismos de financiamiento local para respaldar los requisitos de 
aportación para subvenciones, el desarrollo de proyectos y otras necesidades de 
financiamiento no federal. La discusión incluirá el modelo de Waco y otros enfoques 
comparables que puedan ayudar al MPO a evaluar un marco de contribución local anual 
predecible. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar los hallazgos al Comité de 
Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
8. Recibir una actualización sobre la adquisición de espacio de oficina y la autoridad de 
negociación de arrendamientos. 

Discusión y recomendación: 
El personal proporcionará una actualización sobre el contrato de arrendamiento actual de la 
oficina del MPO, el tiempo de expiración y la necesidad de evaluar opciones disponibles de 
espacio público y privado para continuar las operaciones del MPO. La discusión incluirá el 
estado de la adquisición y la autoridad de negociación de arrendamientos previamente 
discutida por el Comité de Política de Transporte. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar los hallazgos al Comité de 
Política de Transporte según corresponda. 
9. Seguimiento y discusión sobre la lista completa de proyectos del BORRADOR del Programa 
de Transporte Metropolitano (MTP). 
Discusión y recomendación: 
El personal proporcionará información adicional sobre la lista de proyectos del Borrador del 
Plan de Transporte Metropolitano. Las listas de proyectos del MTP se revisan periódicamente 
para asegurar que los proyectos incluidos sigan siendo actuales, reflejen las necesidades de 
transporte regional y permanezcan consistentes con los requisitos de planificación aplicables 
de TxDOT y del gobierno federal. 
Acción solicitada: Solo discusión. No se requiere acción. Informar los hallazgos al Comité de 
Política de Transporte según corresponda.

established local funding mechanisms to support grant match requirements, project 
development, and other non-federal funding needs. The discussion will include the Waco 
model and other comparable approaches that may assist the MPO in evaluating a 
predictable annual local contribution framework. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate.
