Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide an update on the current MPO office lease, expiration timing, and the 
need to evaluate available public and private space options for continued MPO 
operations. The discussion will include the status of procurement and lease negotiation 
authority previously discussed by the Transportation Policy Committee. 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
9. 
Follow up and discussion regarding the DRAFT Metropolitan Transportation Program 
(MTP) full project list. 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide additional information regarding the Draft Metropolitan Transportation 
Plan project list. MTP project lists are reviewed periodically to ensure that listed projects 
remain current, reflect regional transportation needs, and remain consistent with 
applicable TxDOT and federal planning requirements. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion only. No action required. Report findings to the 
Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate.

Lubbock Power & Light Overview 
 
Mission and Purpose 
The purpose of Lubbock Power and Light (LP&L) is “the provision of dependable and reliable electric service at reasonable 
and competitive rates to the citizens of Lubbock while being financially self-sustaining.” (Lubbock City Charter) The mission 
of Lubbock Power & Light is to deliver reliable and resilient utility services through the effective operation and maintenance 
of: 
 
LP&L: Electric transmission, distribution, substation, market, outage call center, metering, billing, and revenue 
management systems. 
 
COLU (City of Lubbock Utilities): Water, wastewater, solid waste and storm water utilities customer service call 
center, metering, billing, and revenue management systems. 
 
Strategic Plan 
Vision: To be the leading municipally owned utility, consistently delivering exceptional system delivery services and ensuring 
customer satisfaction. LP&L is dedicated to true business sustainability through forward-thinking innovation, data-driven and 
risk informed decision-making, and a commitment to employee respect while effectively addressing customer needs. 
 
Strategy: To foster a culture of innovation, safety, and excellence. We strive to build a performance-driven environment with 
a target of zero safety incidents, accidents, or failures. This commitment is achieved by empowering employees and 
leadership to be open-minded, adaptable, fast-paced, resilient, and skilled in implementing effective and timely innovations 
and technologies. 
 
Objective 1: Deliver exceptional customer value by optimizing operations for efficiency, reliability, and responsiveness across 
all service touchpoints. As industry leaders in operational management, we strive to be the employer of choice by fostering 
innovation, prioritizing safety, and investing in our people, technology, and equipment. Our commitment to excellence drives 
us to continuously improve while staying true to our mission and purpose. 
 
Performance Measure: Employee Lost Time Incidents 
 
Performance Measure: Employee Injury Rate 
 
Performance Measure: System Outage Call Center Activity – Total calls and handling time. 
 
Performance Measure: System Outage Calls vs. Wait Time 
 
System Delivery Rates compared with other TDU’s - Annually 
 
Objective 2: Achieve operational excellence through investment and improvements in grid reliability and resilience, 
leveraging advanced technologies and proactive risk management. 
 
Performance Measure: Average Customer Outage Restoration Time – “Customer Average Interruption Duration 
Index (CAIDI)” 
 
Performance Measure Average System Outage Restoration Time – “System Average Interruption Duration Index 
(SAIDI)” 
 
Performance Measure: “System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI)” 
 
Objective 3: Strengthen financial resilience and long-term sustainability by leveraging advanced analytics, dynamic reporting, 
and integrated enterprise risk management (ERM). We deliver timely, accurate, and insightful decision-making information 
to the Board and Executive staff to drive strategic success. 
 
Performance Measure: Days Cash on Hand 
 
Performance Measure: Debt Service Reserve Ratio 
 
Performance Measure: Debt/Asset Ratio 
 
Performance Measure: ERM Inventory Top 10 score 
 
Accomplishments for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 
 
Applied for a Department of Energy SPARK Grant to support transmission system upgrades and system 
modernization projects. 
 
Reduced average outage restoration time from 66 minutes to 50 minutes through operational improvements. 
 
Completed ARC Flash Project in accordance with the NFPA 70E to improve employee safety. 
 
Completed engineering design work for upgrades at Erskine Substation to support future load growth.

Lubbock Power & Light Overview 
 
 
Completed design and construction of multiple distribution system upgrades identified in 15-year plan, including 
three reconductors to support improve reliability and capacity. 
 
Continued work to eliminate legacy 4 kV infrastructure to improve system safety and reliability. 
 
Developed a GIS data model for LP&L’s fiber optic network to improve management and planning. 
 
Supported ERCOT weatherization inspection resulting in full compliance. 
 
Completed phase one of the router replacement initiative, upgrading network infrastructure and improving system

 
Established a maintenance program to inspect and perform preventative maintenance on “trouble circuits” 
improving overall system reliability. 
 
Completed multiple feeder line buildouts and two reconductoring projects to improve load balancing and support 
future growth. 
 
Advanced SCADA/EMS upgrade to improve system monitoring and control capabilities. 
 
Advanced deployment and evaluation of cybersecurity tools. 
 
Enhanced cybersecurity through system scanning and implementation of recommended improvements.

Installed backup servers to improve system resiliency and reduce risk of service interruption.

Management of Fire Hydrant account processes

Joint ownership between Customer Service & Revenue Management of the Water Adjustment process 
 
Objectives for FY 2026-27 
 
Implement Governance, Risk, and Compliance platform to strength compliance and oversight. 
 
Continue design and begin construction of West Loop Transmission Project. 
 
Implement an Enterprise Risk Management program to identify and mitigate system and operational risks. 
 
Continue conversion of the legacy 4KV infrastructure to improve reliability and reduce system risks. 
 
Begin preparation for replacement of the Posey T2 and Oliver T4 substation transformers. 
 
Complete the fiber upgrade for the Emergency Operations Center and backup control rooms. 
 
Commission Erskine substation and associated feeders to increase capacity in the downtown area. 
 
Begin design of Collier and McCalla substation to support future load growth. 
 
Replace 115kV Breakers across the system to improve reliability. 
 
Continue Northeast Voltage Conversion to expand the 23kV loop to improve reliability and capacity. 
 
Begin deployment of advanced transformer grid monitoring to improve asset visibility and performance monitoring. 
 
Evaluate system impacts of approximately 30 MW of new large customer load. 
 
Evaluate and support implementation of an Asset Management System. 
 
Complete system upgrades between McCollough, Red Raider, and Yellowhouse substations to improve load transfer 
capability and system resiliency. 
 
Complete full ADMS System Replacement to help modernize operations. 
 
Continue optimization of the SCADA/EMS systems to improve system performance, reliability, and usability. 
 
Integrate SCADA/EMS with enterprise systems (OMS, GIS, PI, AMI, CCS, IVR) to enhance operational visibility and 
data-driven decision-making. 
 
Implement Outage Management System and Outage Coordination Software to improve restoration times, crew 
coordination, and customer communication. 
 
Complete implementation of ArcFM/Designer XI and the ESRI Utility Network for improved mapping and system 
modeling. 
 
Complete replacement of remaining field routers to fully optimize the AMI system across the service area. 
 
Support large kW customers in the installation and integration of distributed generation systems utilizing large-scale 
battery storage. 
FY 2026-27 Proposed Operating Budget and Capital Program - 2
Table of Contents

Lubbock Power & Light Overview 
 
 
Advance Phase two of the PowerConnect integration connecting CIS and phone systems to enhance customer 
service efficiency. 
 
Develop proactive customer notification capabilities, including billing, leak alerts, and outage communications to 
improve transparency and customer awareness. 
 
Funding Sources Overview 
Overall, budgeted revenues increased $12.9 million, or 7.4 percent, for FY 2026-27 and include the following changes: 
 
Interest earnings increased $1.2 million, or 74.8 percent, compared to the prior budget of $1.6 million, reflecting 
higher expected yields in the pooled investment portfolio due to a sustained higher short-term interest rate 
environment consistent with broader economic expectations. 
 
Distribution System Revenue decreased $3.1 million, or 2.4 percent, due to lower-than-anticipated electric 
consumption based on historical load. This revenue was derived from a cost-of-service study “COS”. The revenue 
requirement for operational costs shifted significantly as the Utility transitioned to a delivery only provider in the 
retail market. These revenues will cover the operational costs of the Utility as a Transmission & Distribution Utility 
(TDU). 
 
FFE revenues decreased $0.1 million, or 0.6 percent, due to a slight decrease in projected load. The FFE revenue is 
calculated as a “cents-per-kilowatt hour” (¢/kWh). 
 
TCOS revenues decreased $0.2 million, or 0.5 percent. The TCOS rate filing incorporates all the transmission assets 
related to the ERCOT integration, along with the appropriate FFEs, and is approved by the PUC. Final TCOS revenues 
are subject to PUC approval and could be higher or lower than the forecast. Of those TCOS revenues, $2.1 million is 
split into a line item in the expense section that properly accounts for the collection of FFE funds that will be passed 
through to the City. 
 
ERCOT Hold Harmless Credit totals $7.3 million and is an offset to TCOS revenues. In PUC Docket No. 47576, the 
order approving LP&L’s initial integration into ERCOT, the PUC required LP&L to pay $22.0 million each year for the 
first five years, which will be credited to ERCOT wholesale transmission customers to mitigate integration costs. This 
amount is shown as an offset to TCOS revenues in the model. Payments began in February 2022 and will continue 
monthly until January 2027. The $14.7 million, or 66.7 percent, decrease to the credit reflects the FY 2026-27 budget 
capturing only the remaining four months of payments under the original schedule. 
 
Fees and Charges increased by $0.2 million, or 13.3 percent. This is due to the continued collection of Disconnect 
and Reconnect service fees. This increase is based on current and prior year collection trends and adjusted for 
expected activity levels. 
 
Outside Work Orders and Street Lights increased by $1.8 million, or 121.1 percent, primarily due to the anticipated 
payment for requests for interconnect studies. This increase is offset by expenses in the engineering cost center for 
the completion of the studies. 
 
Miscellaneous Revenues decreased $1.7 million, due to one-time subrogation revenue from insurance proceeds 
from the Brandon Substation damages. 
 
Expense Overview 
Budgeted expenses increased $19.2 million, or 10.6 percent, for FY 2026-27. These changes are detailed in the following 
sections: 
 
Compensation increased $0.6 million, or 2.6 percent, primarily due to a three percent cost of living adjustment 
(COLA) totaling $0.6 million. LP&L will align its COLA with the City’s non-civil service adjustment, provided the 
adjustment is not less than 2 percent. 
 
Benefits increased $0.2 million, or 2.3 percent, driven primarily by a $0.4 million increase in health benefit costs and 
the impact of the three percent COLA, these increases were offset by a $0.2 million decrease in TMRS. 
 
Supplies increased by $0.1 million or 9.8 percent primarily due to a $0.1 million increase in safety supplies. 
 
Transmission increased by $2.9 million or 7.1 percent, primarily due to an increase in the postage stamp rate in line 
with overall ERCOT 4CP system load growth. 
 
Maintenance costs increased by $0.5 million, or 13.9 percent, due to an increase of $0.3 million in maintenance of 
overhead lines in distribution cost center, a $0.1 increase in maintenance underground lines, and a $0.1 million 
increase in vehicle maintenance.

Consider approval of the May 19, 2026, Transportation Policy Committee meeting minutes.

Approve. 
 
6. 
Review and Take Action Regarding Grant Development, Grant Application Authority, and Federal 
Funding Strategy 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will present a summary of currently available and recurring federal funding opportunities 
relevant to projects identified in the Metropolitan Transportation Plan, 10 Year Plan, Transportation 
Improvement Program, and related multimodal regional priorities. Staff will also discuss the 
compressed timeframes that now characterize many discretionary grant programs and request 
direction regarding authority to evaluate, prepare, and submit time sensitive applications when those 
applications are consistent with adopted MPO plans and priorities. 
 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of staff authority to pursue and submit qualifying grant applications and related 
letters of support, subject to subsequent reporting to the Transportation Policy Committee. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approval 
 
7. 
Review and Take Action Regarding MPO Bylaws Review and Creation of a Subcommittee 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will present an overview of current MPO governance documents, recent state and federal 
coordination regarding MPO administration, and the need to distinguish between structural 
compliance items, policy choices, and housekeeping revisions within the bylaws. 
 
Action Required: 
Consider approval to establish a Bylaws subcommittee and direct staff to begin the review process. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve 
 
8. 
Receive a Report on Renewal and Revision of the Planning Agreement Between TxDOT, the Lubbock 
Metropolitan Planning Organization, and the Fiscal Agent 

Discussion: 
Staff will present an update regarding the draft statewide metropolitan planning agreement, the prior 
extension of the existing agreement, and the need for timely LMPO review and comment before 
return to TxDOT. 
 
Action Required: 
 Receive Report. 
 
9. 
Review and Take Action Regarding Office Space Procurement and Lease Negotiation Authority 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will present an update on the current office lease, expiration timing, and the need to evaluate 
public and private space options for continued MPO operations. Staff requests authority to investigate 
options, negotiate terms, and return a recommended agreement as appropriate. 
 
Action Required:

recommended agreement to the Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate.

relevant to projects identified in the Metropolitan Transportation Plan, 10 Year Plan, Transportation 
Improvement Program, and related multimodal regional priorities. Staff will also discuss the 
compressed timeframes that now characterize many discretionary grant programs and request 
direction regarding authority to evaluate, prepare, and submit time sensitive applications when those 
applications are consistent with adopted MPO plans and priorities. 
 
Action Required: 
Consider approval of staff authority to pursue and submit qualifying grant applications and related 
letters of support, subject to subsequent reporting to the Transportation Policy Committee. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approval 
 
7. 
Review and Take Action Regarding MPO Bylaws Review and Creation of a Subcommittee 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will present an overview of current MPO governance documents, recent state and federal 
coordination regarding MPO administration, and the need to distinguish between structural 
compliance items, policy choices, and housekeeping revisions within the bylaws. 
 
Action Required: 
Consider approval to establish a Bylaws subcommittee and direct staff to begin the review process. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve 
 
8. 
Receive a Report on Renewal and Revision of the Planning Agreement Between TxDOT, the Lubbock 
Metropolitan Planning Organization, and the Fiscal Agent 

Discussion: 
Staff will present an update regarding the draft statewide metropolitan planning agreement, the prior 
extension of the existing agreement, and the need for timely LMPO review and comment before 
return to TxDOT. 
 
Action Required: 
 Receive Report. 
 
9. 
Review and Take Action Regarding Office Space Procurement and Lease Negotiation Authority 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will present an update on the current office lease, expiration timing, and the need to evaluate 
public and private space options for continued MPO operations. Staff requests authority to investigate 
options, negotiate terms, and return a recommended agreement as appropriate. 
 
Action Required: 
Consider approval authorizing the Executive Director to evaluate office space options, negotiate 
prospective lease terms or extensions, enter and sign a future agreement after returning the 
recommended agreement to the Transportation Policy Committee as appropriate. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve 
 
10.

April 2026.

disponibles y recurrentes relevantes para los proyectos identificados en el Plan Metropolitano de 
Transporte, el Plan Decimal Anual, el Programa de Mejora del Transporte y las prioridades 
regionales multimodales relacionadas. El personal también discutirá los plazos reducidos que ahora 
caracterizan muchos programas de subvenciones discrecionales y solicitará orientación sobre la 
autoridad para evaluar, preparar y presentar solicitudes sensibles al tiempo cuando dichas 
solicitudes sean coherentes con los planes y prioridades adoptados de la MPO.

records.summary: City of Lubbock, Texas Library Board Meeting June 15th, at 12:00 PM Mahon Community Room 1306 9th St, Lubbock, TX 79407 1) Call to Order Welcome and introductions – Patricia Maloney 2) Minutes Consider the approval of the May 18th, 2026 meeting minutes. 3) Citizen Comments According to City of Lubbock Board Rules, any citizen wishing to appear before a regular meeting of the Libra
records.text:
City of Lubbock, Texas 
Library Board Meeting 
June 15th, at 12:00 PM 
Mahon Community Room 
1306 9th St, Lubbock, TX 79407 
 
1) Call to Order 
Welcome and introductions – Patricia Maloney 
 
2) Minutes 
Consider the approval of the May 18th, 2026 meeting minutes. 
 
3) Citizen Comments 
According to City of Lubbock Board Rules, any citizen wishing to appear before a regular meeting of the 
Library Board, regarding any matter posted on the Library Board Agenda below, shall complete the sign-up 
form provided at the meeting, no later than 12:00 p.m. Any citizen wishing to comment on any matter posted on 
the Library Board agenda below that will not be in attendance in person may submit a citizen comment by email 
at HStewart@mylubbock.us, no later than 8:00 a.m. on the date of the meeting. Submitted comments must 
include name and address. Each comment will be read aloud for a period of time not to exceed three minutes 
pursuant to City of Lubbock Board Rules. Citizen Comments is an opportunity for citizens to make comments 
and express a position on agenda items. Any comment received that is in the nature of asking a question will be 
referred to an appropriate member of the library or City staff for a response and will not be read aloud at the 
meeting. In accordance with the Texas Open Meetings Act, the Libraries Board may not take action on public 
matters during Citizen Comments. 
 
4) Presentations 
 4.1) Meet the Staff-Patterson Branch Library 
 4.2) Lubbock Library Director Report – Hannah Stewart, Lubbock Library Director 
 4.3) FOL President Report – Lynne Strickland, FOL Chair 
 4.4) Genealogical Society Report- Kathy Kitten 

5) Work Session 
 5.1) Discussion – A discussion pertaining to housekeeping items and future meeting agenda items. 
 
 5.2) Next regularly scheduled meeting will be at noon on August 17th, 2026 at the Mahon Library. There is no 
board meeting in July. 

Lubbock Libraries Board meetings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact the City of 
Lubbock at 806-775-2826 or write to 1306 9th Street, Lubbock, TX 79401 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

Staff Recommendation: 
Approve. 
 
6. 
Judge Parish to address the Transportation Policy Committee regarding matters impacting MPO’s 
throughout the state. 
 
7. 
FY 2025–2026 Unified Planning Work Program (UPWP) – Proposed Amendment and Public Hearing 
 
Discussion: 
Following the assessment and public hearing by the Transportation Advisory Committee, staff 
submits the proposed adjustment to the FY 2025-2026 UPWP. The amendment eliminates certain 
Task 5 activities that no longer align with current federal eligibility, regional priorities, or staffing 
capacity, and redirects those resources to the development of standard operating procedures, 
standardized engineering processes, and implementation-ready planning tools. The objective is to 
ensure that future MPO work with federal funds adheres to current TxDOT guidance and federal 
requirements. 
 
Action Required: 
Approval and adoption by resolution 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Approve as recommended by the Transportation Advisory Committee. 
 
8. 
Unified Transportation Plan (UTP) and 10 Yr Plan Review 
 
Discussion: 
Staff will provide an update on the requirements for the next Unified Transportation Plan (UTP) and 
10 Year Plan, their purpose, and how they relate to the Transportation Improvement Program. 
 
Action Required: 
No action required 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve as recommended by the Transportation Advisory Committee. 

9. 
Defense Community Infrastructure Program (DCIP) 
Discussion: 
The staff will present an overview of a proposed grant application for the Defense Community 
Infrastructure Program (DCIP), which is a competitive grant designed to address community 
deficiencies that support military installation readiness and lethality. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval for the MPO to pursue the Defense Community Infrastructure Program grant 
application. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve as recommended by the Transportation Advisory Committee. 

10. 
Railroad Crossing Elimination Program (RCE) 
Discussion: 
The staff will present an overview of a proposed Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) program to 
fund highway-rail or pathway-rail grade crossing improvements. This program is focused on 
improving the safety and mobility of people and goods. 
Action Required: 
Consider approval for the MPO to submit an application to the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) 
for Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) funding. 
 
Staff Recommendation: 
Staff Recommendation: Approve to proceed with the application and submission.

March 2026.

Discusión: 
Tras la evaluación y audiencia pública del Comité Asesor de Transporte, el personal presenta el 
ajuste propuesto al UPWP del año fiscal 2025-2026. La enmienda elimina ciertas actividades de la 
Tarea 5 que ya no se alinean con la elegibilidad federal actual, las prioridades regionales o la 
capacidad de personal, y redirige esos recursos al desarrollo de procedimientos operativos estándar, 
procesos de ingeniería estandarizados y herramientas de planificación listas para implementar. El 
objetivo es asegurar que el trabajo futuro de MPO con fondos federales cumpla con las directrices 
actuales de TxDOT y los requisitos federales.

1.

2.
Public Comment. Public comment is an opportunity for the public to make comments and
express a position on agenda items.
a.
This period, of up to thirty minutes, is dedicated to public comment. Each member
of the public will have three minutes to speak. Any member of the public that
requires the assistance of a translator will have six minutes to speak. Comments
must be limited to only those items posted on the Electric Utility Board agenda.
Any member of the public wishing to speak shall sign up on the public comment
sheet on the day of the Electric Utility Board Meeting, prior to the beginning of the
meeting. The Electric Utility Board shall follow the order of persons wishing to
speak as listed on the sign-up sheet. If everyone who signed up to speak has been
given an opportunity to speak and the time designated for public comment has not
been exhausted, the Electric Utility Board may, at its discretion, open the floor to
anyone else wishing to address the Electric Utility Board, subject to all the same
procedures and guidelines.
3.
The Electric Utility Board may make any comments related to board member activities,
events, community engagement, or current or future agenda items.

Executive Session

§552.133, and §552.1331 to discuss and deliberate, on the following competitive matters
of Lubbock Power & Light, reasonably related to the following categories:
(i) Discussion and deliberation of generation matters, including but not limited to
generation unit and/or portfolio sale opportunities including the potential for unused
land designated for other uses;
(ii) Discussion of risk management, contracts, and strategies, customer billing, and usage
information, system load characteristics, and ERCOT power analyses and strategies;

for which the public power utility is the sole certificated retail provider);

including amounts billed or collected for utility usage

seeking the advice of legal counsel about pending or contemplated litigation or settlement

11:30 a.m. – Approximately - Following completion of the Executive Session, the Electric 
Utility Board will reconvene in open session to discuss the items listed below. It is anticipated 
that the open session will begin at 11:30 a.m. However, this is an approximation and the Board 
may begin the open session earlier or later depending on when the Executive Session is 
complete. 
Open Session 
8.
Approve the minutes from the Regular Electric Utility Board meeting held on April 21, 
2026.
9.
Presentation and discussion of the update/report by the LP&L Chief Administrative 
Officer, or his designee, regarding strategic planning, board committee reports, association 
matters, ordinance change requests, EUB policy and procedures, customer service, 
business center practices, procedures and policies, transition to retail customer choice, 
customer concerns and complaints, billing system, forms and procedures, status of 
transmission and distribution projects, generation, mutual aid, weather events, outage and 
restoration efforts, grid matters, Electric Reliability Council of Texas (“ERCOT”) matters 
and committee participation, staffing levels, personnel, regulatory matters, training, 
cybersecurity, mutual aid agreement, and operational performance metrics.
10.
Presentation and discussion of financial and capital statements, budget, financing options, 
audits, and financial policies of Lubbock Power & Light relating to debt issuance issues 
and historical debt matters, reserve account funding, cost allocation, revenue and expense 
projections, customer metering, tariff and billing, service and administrative issues, and 
risk management information including rates. 
Consent 
11.
Consider a resolution authorizing the Chief Administrative Officer or his designee to 
execute a Professional Services Agreement (Agreement) by and between the City of 
Lubbock, acting by and through Lubbock Power & Light, for Independent Representative 
(Owner’s Engineering) Services with Electrical Consultants, Inc. (ECI). This will be a four-
year agreement with a not-to-exceed of Five Million, Two Hundred Thousand Dollars and 
zero/100 dollars ($5,200,000.00).
12.
Consider a resolution authorizing the Chief Administrative Officer, or his designee, to 
execute Professional Service Agreement by and between the City of Lubbock, acting by 
and through Lubbock Power & Light, and 1898 and Co., of Kansas City, Missouri, Request 
for Proposal (RFP) 7105-26-ELD - LP&L Operations Software Implementation Program 
Consulting Services. This agreement for $1,590,000.00 ELD - LP&L Operations Software 
Implementation Program Consulting Services. This agreement for $1,590,000.00 includes 
change order language of up to 20% of the NTE may be authorized by the Chief 
Administrative Officer, notwithstanding his purchasing authority will be for a term of 36 
3 of 119
Back to Agenda

months with the option to extend an additional two (2) one-year extensions of time so long 
as the amount of the consideration payable hereunder does not increase. This agreement 
includes professional and project management services, guidance and oversight for 
Geographic Information System (GIS) upgrade, implementation of a new Work Asset 
Management System, and the implementation of a new Advanced Distribution 
Management System (ADMS). 
13.
Consider a resolution appointing and authorizing the Chief Administrative Officer to act
as the Authorized Representative for all Lubbock Power & Light filings with the Electric
Reliability Council of Texas, appointing and authorizing the Chief Operating Officer and
the Chief Compliance Officer to act as the Back-up Authorized Representative(s), and
superseding and replacing Resolution No. EUB 2025-R0007 regarding the previous
Authorized Representative and Back-up Authorized Representative for ERCOT.
14.
Consider a resolution authorizing the Purchasing Manager, or his designee, to execute
Purchase Order, by and between the City of Lubbock, acting by and through Lubbock
Power & Light and Itron Inc., of Liberty Lake, Washington, for $531,138.00 with a 15
week delivery, Invitation to Bid (ITB) 7125-26-ELD - Cisco Heavy Duty Routers
Preloaded with Itron OpenWay Riva Program. Cisco IR8140 router is the replacement for
the Cisco CGR1240 that was discontinued. Four IR8140 routers have already been
purchased and installed. To complete the replacement project, an additional 40 IR8140
routers are required. This quantity will allow for the replacement of the remaining units
and provide two spare IR8140 routers for emergency use.
15.
Consider a resolution rejecting all bids for Request for Proposal (RFP) 7123-26-ELD -
Oliver Substation 50 MVA Transformer Repair Facility Services. Proposal submitted
exceeded the cost of the unit, LP&L will look at replacing the unit with a new transformer.
16.
Adjourn.

City of Lubbock, Texas 
Library Board Meeting 
May 18th, at 12:00 PM 
Mahon Community Room 
1306 9th St, Lubbock, TX 79407 
 
1) Call to Order 
Welcome and introductions – Sheri Lewis 
 
2) Minutes 
Consider the approval of the April 20th, 2026 meeting minutes. 
 
3) Citizen Comments 
According to City of Lubbock Board Rules, any citizen wishing to appear before a regular meeting of the 
Library Board, regarding any matter posted on the Library Board Agenda below, shall complete the sign-up 
form provided at the meeting, no later than 12:00 p.m. Any citizen wishing to comment on any matter posted on 
the Library Board agenda below that will not be in attendance in person may submit a citizen comment by email 
at HStewart@mylubbock.us, no later than 8:00 a.m. on the date of the meeting. Submitted comments must 
include name and address. Each comment will be read aloud for a period of time not to exceed three minutes 
pursuant to City of Lubbock Board Rules. Citizen Comments is an opportunity for citizens to make comments 
and express a position on agenda items. Any comment received that is in the nature of asking a question will be 
referred to an appropriate member of the library or City staff for a response and will not be read aloud at the 
meeting. In accordance with the Texas Open Meetings Act, the Libraries Board may not take action on public 
matters during Citizen Comments. 
 
4) Presentations 
 4.1) Meet the Staff 
 4.2) Lubbock Library Director Report – Hannah Stewart, Lubbock Library Director 
 4.3) FOL President Report – Lynne Strickland, FOL Chair 
 4.4) Genealogical Society Report- Kathy Kitten 

5) Work Session 
 5.1) Discussion – A discussion pertaining to housekeeping items and future meeting agenda items. 
 
 5.2) Next regularly scheduled meeting will be at noon on June 15th, 2026 at the Mahon Library. 

Lubbock Libraries Board meetings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact the City of 
Lubbock at 806-775-2826 or write to 1306 9th Street, Lubbock, TX 79401 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

Members of the public may comment on items listed on the agenda. Comments are 
limited to three minutes per speaker. 
 
5. 
Consider approval of the April 2nd, 2026, meeting minutes for the Transportation 
Advisory Committee. 
 
6. 
Unified Transportation Plan (UTP) and 10 Yr Plan Review 
 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide an update on the requirements for the next Unified Transportation Plan 
(UTP) and 10 Year Plan, their purpose, and how they relate to the Transportation 
Improvement Program. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion, report findings to the Transportation Policy Committee. 

7. 
Local Funding Mechanism 
 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
Staff will provide a case study overview of how an MPO has developed a local fund for non-
federalized grant matching. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion, report findings to the Transportation Policy Committee. 
 
8. 
Defense Community Infrastructure Program (DCIP) 
 
Discussion and Recommendation: 

The staff will present an overview of a proposed grant application for the Defense 
Community Infrastructure Program (DCIP), which is a competitive grant designed to 
address community deficiencies that support military installation readiness and lethality. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion and recommend advancing to the Transportation Policy 
Committee for staff to pursue the Defense Community Infrastructure Program. 

9. 
Railroad Crossing Elimination Grant (RCE) 
 
Discussion and Recommendation: 
 
The staff will present an overview of a proposed Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) 
program to fund highway-rail or pathway-rail grade crossing improvements. This 
program is focused on improving the safety and mobility of people and goods. 
 
Action Requested: Discussion and recommend approval to the Transportation Policy 
Committee for staff to pursue the Railroad Crossing Elimination.

de Transporte.

Plan deportivo UnifiedTran (UTP) y revisión del plan a 10 años 
 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El personal proporcionará una actualización sobre los requisitos para el próximo Plan 
Unificado de Transporte (UTP) y el Plan Decimal Anual, su propósito y cómo se relacionan 
con elPrograma de Mejora de Transporte. 
 
Se solicita acción: Discusión, informe de las conclusiones al Comité de Política de 
Transporte.

Mecanismo de financiación local 
 
Debate y recomendaciones: 
 
El personal proporcionará una visión general del estudio de caso de cómo una MPO ha 
desarrollado un fondo local para la igualación de subvenciones no federalizadas. 
 
Se solicita acción: Discusión, informe de las conclusiones al Comité de Política de 
Transporte.

Programa de Infraestructura Comunitaria de Defensa (DCIP) 
 
Debate y recomendaciones: 

El personal presentará una visión general de una solicitud de subvención propuesta 
para el Programa de Infraestructura Comunitaria de Defensa (DCIP), que es una 
subvención competitiva diseñada para abordar las diferenciascomunitarias que apoyan 
la preparación y letalidad de las instalaciones militares. 
 
Se solicita acción: Discusión y recomendación de avance al Comité de Política de

City of Lubbock, Texas 
Centerpointe Public Improvement District 
Public Hearing for the Proposed Centerpointe Public Improvement District 
May 12, 2026 at 2:00 P.M. 
Citizens Tower, Council Chambers 
 
Please take notice that on May 12, 2026, at 2:00 PM, the City Council of Lubbock, Texas, will conduct a public 
hearing in the City Council Chamber of Citizens Tower at 1314 Avenue K, Lubbock, TX 79401. The purpose of this 
hearing is to consider the establishment of the Centerpointe Public Improvement District (“District”) pursuant to 
Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code (The “Act”). 
 
All interested persons will be given the opportunity to appear and be heard at such public hearing. Written or oral 
objections will be considered. The hearing may be adjourned from time to time until the City Council makes findings 
by ordinance as to the advisability of the District. 
 
The following information is hereby provided concerning the matters to be considered at such hearing: 
 
Nature of the Services and Improvements: The general nature of the proposed public improvements is: (i) 
acquisition, construction, or drainage facilities or improvements, (a) the design, construction and maintenance of 
parks and green spaces, together with any ancillary structures, features or amenities such as playgrounds, splash pads, 
pool(s), athletic facilities, pavilions, community facilities, irrigation, walkways, lighting, benches, trash receptacles 
and any similar items located there in along with all necessary grading, drainage, and similar infrastructure involved 
in the construction of such parks and greens; landscaping, hardscaping and irrigation; and (ii) payment of costs 
associated with developing and financing the public improvements listed in subdivision (i) including costs of 
establishing, administering and operating the District. 
 
Estimated Cost of the Services and Improvements: The proposed assessment for the first year is for tax year 2026 
which will fund the budget for FY 2026-27. The total estimated cost of services provided by the District is estimated 
at $168,534 over the next five years. The estimated annual cost rises from $0 in the first year to $72,320 in year five 
(5). The costs are based on a proposed assessment rate of $0.17 per $100.00 of valuation through tax year 2031. 
 
Boundaries: The proposed boundaries of the Centerpointe Public Improvement District (PID) cover a portion of an 
area in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas, generally bounded on the east by North Avenue U, on the south 
by Drake Street, on the west by North University, and on the north by Georgetown Street. 
 
Method of Assessment: Properties will be assessed based on the City’s “net taxable value” as established by the 
Lubbock Central Appraisal District. Each assessment will be determined using the formula: (net taxable value 
divided by 100) multiplied by assessment rate. 
 
Apportionment of Cost: The District is to supplement and enhance services within the District, but not replace or 
supplant existing City services provided within the District. One hundred percent of the maintenance of the public 
improvements and any construction of new public improvements included in the Service Plan will be funded by the 
Public Improvement District. 
 
Public hearings are available to all persons regardless of disability. If you require special assistance, please contact 
the City Secretary’s Office at 775-2025 or write to P.O. Box 2000, Lubbock, Texas, 79457, at least 48 hours in 
advance of the public hearing. 
 
Any questions concerning the matters described in this notice should be directed to: Molly Ballesteros, City of 
Lubbock Business Development Department at 775-3083.
